extracted.intended_audience: aspiring/new writers planning to submit novels to literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and sending novel submissions (covering letter, pitch, synopsis, CV) to literary agents, focused on what agents look for and common submission mistakes. Emphasises presentation, brevity, relevance, and agent-research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Good writing is the best way to grab our attention. We are not interested in tricks, gimmicks or marketing ideas. If you write well, you will stand out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise craft and voice over gimmicks; a well-written manuscript is the primary route to interest from agents. Avoid relying on marketing hooks in the submission itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading: no grammatical or spelling mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: We don't take kindly to grammatical and spelling mistakes. Make sure you proofread your work before submitting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully copy-edit and proofread all submission materials (sample pages, synopsis, cover letter). Errors signal carelessness and can harm your chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, punchy pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch your book concisely, elegantly, punchily. Avoid too many adverbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a tight, engaging pitch that communicates the core of the book quickly. Edit for economy and strong verbs; eliminate unnecessary adverbs and padding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short, to-the-point synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your synopsis short and to the point. We want a glimpse into your story and an idea of the plot and characters, not a five-page blow-by-blow account of each chapter and scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an overview of themes, main plot arc, and key characters without scene-by-scene detail. The novel itself is for the full narrative; the synopsis should summarise rather than narrate every beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopses vs blurbs distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't confuse a synopsis with a blurb. A synopsis is an outline of the book's themes and plot. A blurb is written by the publisher to attract readers to the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write a promotional blurb as your synopsis. Avoid marketing adjectives in the synopsis — e.g., blurb-like words such as 'exhilarating' and 'exquisite' do not belong in a synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disingenuous self-deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid disingenuous self-deprecation in a covering letter (‘I know you won’t have the time for a lowly writer like me...’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present yourself professionally and with appropriate confidence. Self-deprecating remarks can undermine the author's perceived seriousness and value their work less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the agent's list and spell names correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Show knowledge of the agent's existing list – and spell their authors’ names correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the agent's current authors and titles; reference them accurately in your letter. Misspelling an author's name indicates poor research and carelessness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading 'X meets Y' comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pitching your book as something meets something else as you might send the agent down the wrong path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use comparative descriptions, ensure they accurately reflect tone/market rather than creating misleading expectations. Poor comps can misposition your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Your pitch/cover letter should be no longer than a page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the covering letter concise and focused—one page maximum. Use that space to state the book, word count, relevant credits/referral, and a short pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not brag, but highlight distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not wise to brag. Let the agent be the judge of the quality of the material. But do highlight in your covering letter why you think your book is distinctive and special.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid boastful language or claims about being 'the best'. Instead, succinctly explain what makes the book different (hook, theme, protagonist, unusual research) without hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify target audience and appropriate comps
rubrics_metrics.description: Think carefully about who your target audience is and what books your work would sit alongside – don't just randomly pick an author we represent in an attempt to flatter us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic comparable titles that genuinely match your book's readership and tone. Flattering or irrelevant comps harm credibility; choose comps strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not create your own marketing materials or jacket
rubrics_metrics.description: Please don't attempt to fashion your own book jacket cover or marketing material: a team of professionals will address that when your work is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave cover design and marketing copy to publishing professionals; unsolicited mock jackets do not help submissions and may be viewed as inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider whether the idea suits a novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about whether your book idea is suited to be a novel; it might work better as a blog or an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate format fit: some ideas are better served as shorter non-fiction pieces, essays, or serial formats. Ensure the material justifies novel-length treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only include relevant CV information
rubrics_metrics.description: Only send through relevant CV information. We do not need to know about your A-level results, no matter how brilliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pertinent publishing credits, professional experience, and qualifications related to writing; omit irrelevant academic scores or personal trivia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose referrals from publishing contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have been referred to a Curtis Brown agent by a contact at a publishing house please let us know in your letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention professional referrals or recommendations in the cover letter, as these can contextualise the submission and assist consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose prior submissions/contact with the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do mention if you have submitted to or been in touch with one of our agents before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about prior queries or submissions to the agency or its agents; this helps agents track history and avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not respond to rejection arguing the agent is wrong
rubrics_metrics.description: If your work is rejected then please do not reply pointing out that we have made a mistake. Reading is subjective and there are all kinds of reasons for agents turning down proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept rejections professionally. Do not send argumentative replies asserting the agent's mistake; such responses are counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target appropriate agents, avoid random/mass submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Target people who would be appropriate for your work rather than submitting to all agents at Curtis Brown or selecting somebody at random.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor submissions to agents whose lists and tastes align with your book. Mass or random submissions reduce effectiveness and indicate lack of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address submissions to the correct person
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not address a submission to Mr Curtis Brown. He died some time ago. When researching who to submit to, you should have discovered that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the current agent's correct name and title. Outdated or generic salutations show insufficient research and hurt first impressions.
